'''Muzashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (无邪志国造 or むざしのくにのみやつこ) was a {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko}} (provincial governor) that governed the Muzashi Province, which later became the eastern region of {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}}.

The "Kuni no Miyatsuko Chronicle" in {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}} mentions both Muzashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko and {{ill|Q56346583|ja|胸刺国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munagashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q56346583}}. Scholars debate whether these represent one and the same or two separate territories. {{Sfn|Ken Shinokawa|2021|p=}} posits that these were independent clans initially but became united under the nation-building efforts during the {{ill|Taiho|en|Taiho|qid=Q423370|lt=Taihō era}} (702 AD).

== Overview ==

=== Names ===
* '''无謝志国造''' - The name used in {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}.
* '''武蔵国造''' - Later adapted based on the name "Musashi Province."
* '''無邪志国造''' - Modern spelling using {{ill|Simplified Chinese characters|ja|简化字|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Simplified Chinese|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 簡体字|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q185614}}.
* '''牟邪志国造''' - Found in "Kuni no Miyatsuko Chronicle" in various manuscript copies.

=== Founding Ancestors ===
* According to the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, the clan descended from {{ill|Ame no Hohinomi no Mikoto|ja|天之菩卑能命}}, with his son {{ill|Takehiranome|ja|建比良鳥命|zh|建比良鳥命|fr|Takehiranome}} founding Muzashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko.
* The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} attributes the lineage to {{ill|Ame no Hohi|bg|Аме Но Хохи|fa|آمه-نو-هوهی|fr|Ame no Hohi|it|Ame no Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|pl|Niebiański Duch Przewodni|ru|Амэ но Хохи|simple|Ame no Hohi|zh|天菩比神|qid=Q10940685}}.
* The {{ill|Takahashi Ujibumi|en|Takahashi Ujibumi|qid=Q1108567|lt=Takahashi Monjo}} recounts that {{ill|Ōtamahibi|ja|大多毛比}}, who served Emperor {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō}}, was the clan's progenitor.

=== Clan ===
The Muzashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko descended from the {{ill|Musashi clan|ja|武蔵氏}} and shared connections with the {{ill|Izumo clan|ja|出雲氏}}. The following branches are linked:
* {{ill|Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|无邪志国造|qid=Q11504612}}
* {{ill|Q11396372|ja|刑部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakabe clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11396372}}
* {{ill|hasetsukabeuji|ja|丈部氏|qid=Q55530004}}

== Headquarters ==
Primary regions include:
* '''Musashi Province''': Later divided into modern Tokyo, Saitama, and Kanagawa areas.
* '''Mound complexes''': Archaeological evidence suggests their burials were in locations like {{ill|Sakitama Kofun Cluster|en|Sakitama Kofun Cluster|qid=Q2213580|lt=Saitama Kofun Cluster}}.

=== Associated Deities ===
* '''{{ill|Ōkunitama Shrine|en|Ōkunitama Shrine|qid=Q611678|lt=Ōkunitama Shrine}}'''
* '''{{ill|Hikawa Shrine (Saitama)|en|Hikawa Shrine (Saitama)|qid=Q703633|lt=Hikawa Shrine}}'''

== Descendants ==
Their legacy is seen in ancient inscriptions found in tombs and family lineages continuing into the Edo Period.
